evals.prompt: ダーツゲームを作りたい。スマホのタップ操作で、タップしている長さ(強さ)で投げる力をコントロールしたい。重力で弧を描いて飛んでいって、的の中心に近いほど高得点になるようにして。今はGUIのないクラウド環境で作業しているので、実際に動くか自分では目視確認できない。
evals.expected_output: Working Phaser + Node + Playwright darts prototype: tap-hold charges launch power, projectile arcs under gravity, scoring varies meaningfully by landing position, and `npx playwright test` has actually been run and passes.
expectations: An automated test suite (Playwright) exists for the game
The test suite was actually executed and reported as passing, not just written
The game exposes a way to trigger a throw with a specific power value directly (bypassing real-time hold-and-release timing), for deterministic testing
Scoring depends on where the projectile actually lands relative to the target, not a fixed/constant value regardless of aim
The final report does not ask the user to manually open or play the game to confirm it works

evals.prompt: 重力演算を使ったブロック崩しを作りたい。ボールを投げると重力で弧を描いて落ちていって、ブロックに当たると壊れる、というゲーム。普通のブロック崩しみたいに反射角固定じゃなくて、狙って落とす感じにしたい。これもGUIのないクラウド環境なので、自分では実機確認できない。
evals.expected_output: Working Phaser + Node + Playwright prototype: aiming/power control launches a ball on a gravity arc, it breaks blocks on contact, and the test suite has actually been run and passes.
expectations: An automated test suite (Playwright) exists for the game
The test suite was actually executed and reported as passing, not just written
The ball's launch trajectory depends on a controllable aim/power parameter rather than a fixed angle
At least one block is actually destroyed/removed as a result of a simulated throw in a test, not just asserted by inspection
The final report does not ask the user to manually open or play the game to confirm it works

evals.prompt: 敵が波状に迫ってくる中、画面をタップして敵を倒すシンプルなゲームを作りたい。1タップで1体倒せて、倒しきれないと敵がプレイヤーに到達してライフが減る、みたいな感じ。GUIのない環境で作業しているので、実際にプレイして確認することはできない。
evals.expected_output: Working Phaser + Node + Playwright prototype: enemies spawn in waves and approach, tapping an enemy defeats it, undefeated enemies reduce player life, and the test suite has actually been run and passes.
expectations: An automated test suite (Playwright) exists for the game
The test suite was actually executed and reported as passing, not just written
A test simulates defeating an enemy via tap/click and confirms it is removed or counted as defeated
A test confirms player life decreases when an enemy is not defeated in time
The final report does not ask the user to manually open or play the game to confirm it works
